cards.subject: Land of the Lost
lines: The whole zone is a sustained homage to the 1974 series: a family stranded in a dinosaur valley whose defining props were pylons containing coloured crystals.
Williden Marshal and Hol'anyee Marshal are Will and Holly. The camp is Marshal's Refuge. Once you know, the pylons stop being a mechanic and become a quotation.

cards.subject: The crater is a real place
lines: A collapsed volcano whose walls trap an unusually dense population of large animals inside it.
The name and the shape are both lifted from it.
The joke is that the real one works the same way the fake one does.

cards.subject: Nobody explains it
lines: A rainforest sealed inside a crater rim, ringed by Tanaris, Silithus and Uldum.
Everything you will read about titan experiments and petri dishes was written years after this.
In here, nothing in the game accounts for it at all.

cards.subject: The pylons do not teleport you
cards.tag: Three of them, and no fourth
lines: They are crafting stations. Ten crystals of two colours in, one consumable out — a fire bomb, a restore, a ward, a spire.
They only work once a gnome hands you the user's manual.
The vanilla description of them is honest: "The pylons on the ridges of the crater defy explanation."

cards.subject: Linken
lines: A gnome washes ashore with no memory and no interest in gadgets, only swordplay. The chain is named after a line from the 1986 Legend of Zelda.
He says "Excuuuuse me, princess!" and "I'm not used to fighting with other people."
It ends with Linken's Sword of Mastery and Linken's Boomerang.

cards.subject: Larion and Muigin
lines: Two feuding expedition members at the Refuge, one blaming the other for getting them lost.
They are standing next to a Zelda gnome.
Both were shunted into unreachable towers in 4.0.3a. In here you can still talk to them.

cards.subject: Ringo
cards.tag: A Little Help From My Friends
lines: A goblin dying of heat halfway up the volcano, in a south-facing cave.
Walking him out, he faints again and again, and you revive him each time with a borrowed canteen.
His dropped sack is lying outside the cave and finishes a different quest called Lost!

cards.subject: A-Me 01
lines: A mechanical gorilla that speaks in broken English: "Follow... follow A-me. Home."
You escort a robot ape through a valley full of real apes.
She is named for Amy, the signing gorilla in Michael Crichton's Congo, and she was removed from the game in 4.0.3a.

cards.subject: The devilsaurs
lines: They are fifty-five to sixty elites, and King Mosh was the most powerful rare mob in the game before Burning Crusade — rare elite here, downgraded much later.
Devilsaur Leather drops nowhere else in the world.
Which is why the crater was permanently patrolled by people who did not want you in it.

cards.subject: Uhk'loc
lines: A rare gorilla, and the only one of its colour a hunter can tame.
That is the entire reason anyone ever camped that cave.

cards.subject: Lakkari Tar Pits
lines: Lakes of thick black tar with "bones of hundreds of beasts" jutting out of the surface.
It is La Brea with the dinosaurs still standing next to it.
The Tar Lords and Tar Lurkers are the tar itself, walking.

cards.subject: The soil is not for you
lines: Piles of dirt across the crater floor, combined with seeds in a pouch, slowly become Morrowgrain.
It gets handed to the Cenarion Circle for reputation.
This crater is the grind that fed the road to Silithus.

cards.subject: Fire Plume Ridge
lines: A live volcano in the middle of the crater, running shallow enough to heat the geysers on the far side of it.
A goblin has stuck a thermometer into it.
The unit on the dial is degrees Kraklenheit, which he invented.
